item.title: Pete Hegseth’s Department of War backdrop draws comparisons to Nazi imagery on social media
item.description: A redesigned logo and seal immediately set off a wave of unflattering chatter over the weekend. Administration officials say there’s nothing to it. A recent address to the military by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is drawing attention on social media, with users saying the event’s backdrop resembled iconography from the Third Reich.

item.title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
item.description: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to comply with the AI Act. Editing can make the invisible marks harder to detect, it says.

item.title: Trump’s $500 ACA ‘refund’ checks won’t make a dent in rising healthcare costs
item.description: Premiums grew by an average of 18% this year and are expected to grow next year, too. Experts say policy—not onetime payments—is what’s needed. Last week, the Trump administration began sending $500 checks to roughly 1 million Obamacare enrollees in 30 states—a “refund” for what the administration calls “high costs imposed by the Biden administration’s gross mismanagement of Obamacare.”...

item.title: US counties are desperately trying to stop data centers from taking over: A look at how Charlotte, Pima County, and Guildford County are dealing with the onslaught - with an interesting catch
item.description: Guilford, Pima, and Charlotte are all hitting pause on data centers, but the fine print indicates not one of these moratoriums stops a project already in motion.
